title: Classic Lamingtons
description: Aussie pride in a cake cube — built properly, with a real sponge that can hold its own.

method.instruction: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a 20 cm × 30 cm slab pan with baking paper.
In the bowl of a stand mixer, beat eggs and sugar on high speed for 6–8 minutes until pale, thick, and tripled in volume.
Sift flour and baking powder together, then gently fold into the egg mixture in three batches, keeping as much air in the batter as possible.
Heat milk and butter together until melted and warm. Mix a scoop of the batter into the milk mixture, then fold back into the main bowl until just combined.
Pour into the prepared pan and bake for 22–25 minutes or until a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean.
Cool completely on a wire rack. For easier cutting, chill or freeze the sponge briefly.
For the icing: sift icing sugar and cocoa powder into a bowl. Add boiling water and butter. Whisk until smooth. Keep warm while using.
Cut the sponge into 4–5 cm squares.
Dip each square into the warm chocolate icing, letting the excess drip off.
Roll each coated square in desiccated coconut until fully coated.
Set on a wire rack to firm up before serving.

notes.title: Sponge Tips
notes.content: Beat the eggs and sugar until they are genuinely thick and pale — this is what creates the light sponge structure. Fold the flour in gently to keep the air in the batter.

notes.title: Deluxe Version
notes.content: Split each square and fill with raspberry jam and whipped cream for the full bakery-style experience.
